newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Blast may have hit Russian tanker off Japan - Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Blast may have hit Russian tanker off Japan - Moscow.

text.p: An explosion may have caused a Russian tanker to break in two and spill oil off the coast of Japan this month, Interfax news agency quoted Russian Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh as saying on Wednesday.
Preliminary investigation of the wreck of the tanker Nakhodka suggested "there was an external cause due to an explosion", he told a news conference.
Such a blast would help explain why the accident caused such a large oil spill, the minister said.

The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka, a 26-year-old vessel carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of heavy fuel oil from China to Russia, broke in two during stormy weather earlier this month, spilling much of its cargo and polluting rich fishing grounds and Japanese tourist beaches.
The 31-man crew of the tanker was rescued, but the captain is missing and presumed dead.
A full explanation of how the accident occurred will be available only after completion of the investigation, the minister was quoted as saying.
